Just a few days ago Morgan Stanley named the CPO supply chain and put $TSEM in it next to $TSMC and $GFS

Tower announced today a roughly $3 billion silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity expansion in Japan, and the Japanese government is backing about a billion of it in grants, which drops Tower’s net check to around $2 billion. 

They raised their 2028 model to $3.6 billion in revenue and $1.2 billion in net profit. Against $1.6 billion of trailing revenue and $245 million of net income today, that is roughly double the top line and nearly five times the bottom line, at a 33% net margin.

Silicon photonics is the foundry floor of the whole optical buildout, the layer where the photonic chips for co-packaged optics physically get made, and only a handful of merchant fabs on earth can do it at 300mm.

This is the type confirmation I want, a supplier on the scarce floor of the optical stack, a government de-risking the capex, and a company guiding to demand real enough to double itself by 2028.

You don’t commit three billion dollars unless you know that there is a lot more demand headed you way. 

Bullish photonics
